claims.text: A single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy has coercivity below 20 Oe.
Low coercivity in single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti is caused by suppressed orbital moments and weak magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Fe30Co30Ni30Ti10 at.% maintains an fcc structure at room temperature.
Aging Fe-Co-Ni-Ti at 600-800 °C for 1-10 hours can precipitate a Ti-rich Ti2Ni-, TiFe-, or TiNi-type phase.
A 5-15 vol% Ti-rich intermetallic secondary phase can be retained within the fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The proposed Ti-rich precipitates will have sizes of 5-50 nm.
Coherent or semi-coherent Ti-rich precipitates maximize interfacial area with the fcc matrix.
The Ti-rich intermetallic phase may be ferrimagnetic or weakly ferromagnetic.
The Ti-rich phase produces interfacial exchange coupling with the ferromagnetic fcc matrix.
The fcc/intermetallic interface induces local lattice strain and modifies the electronic structure.
Interfacial strain and electronic-structure modification enhance the orbital contribution to magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Ti-rich precipitates pin magnetic domain walls because of their distinct anisotropy and lattice mismatch with the fcc matrix.
Interfacial exchange coupling transfers magnetic anisotropy from the secondary phase to the fcc matrix.
Hybridization between interfacial Ti and Fe, Co, or Ni d-states enhances the orbital moment.
Introducing 5-15 vol% Ti-rich precipitates will raise room-temperature coercivity above 100 Oe.
The modified alloy will retain a Curie temperature above 500 K.
The modified alloy will exhibit a hysteresis-loop squareness ratio greater than 0.5.
Formation of the Ti-rich phase may slightly decrease saturation magnetization.
The proposed hardening mechanism is limited to 5-15 at.% Ti and 5-15 vol% secondary phase.
Excessive Ti can cause transformation to BCC or amorphous structures, while overly coarse precipitates cease to provide effective domain-wall pinning.

contradictions.description: The alloy is called equiatomic or near-equiatomic in Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti, but the example Fe30Co30Ni30Ti10 is strongly depleted in Ti relative to a four-component equiatomic composition.
The stated 77-400 K operating range is described as significantly above room temperature even though most of that interval is below room temperature.
The prediction requires Tc above 500 K, but measurements are specified only up to 400 K, so the proposed experiment cannot directly establish or exclude the 500 K threshold.
